title: TimescaleDB integration: package and continuously test same-database coexistence (TC1)
body:
## Outcome
A synthetic TC1 development experiment on 2026-11-28 found that pg_morlet and TimescaleDB can share a PostgreSQL database for waveform storage, irregular telemetry, compressed derived metrics, exact waveform search and SQL drill-down. This is evidence for an optional integration, not a production support or performance claim.

## Tested versions
- PostgreSQL 17.12, Linux arm64; disposable container limited to 2 CPU / 1 GiB.
- MorletDB release 0.4.0-beta.3, SQL 0.3.14, revision c358bebe8cc24a69eebef0a482d04df597a3194d.
- TimescaleDB 2.31.0, source 4fa2a7c6b579171a1a8966fd87a0d4189ebab43b, full source build including TSL functionality.
- Morlet image digest sha256:897d9b0e62e7320cdcdbbde823f9de33aa6368d6f0461a3b43f08fc0861b095e.
- Combined local image sha256:994f2c53751f573ae6132a2f1eaa9b7541f91e911433238aec17ce23f12de4a2.
- Frozen TC1 protocol SHA-256 ec272c94003669a1b27eaca0106a6878079b69937465c285cd6bec99048fb225.

## Observed
1. Both extension installation orders passed fresh append/read + hypertable checks.
2. Repeating [-0.0, 1, -1, 2] for 1024 samples read back bit-exactly, including signed zero. Statistics matched independent expectations: mean 0.5, RMS sqrt(1.5).
3. Waveform + metric writes in one transaction rolled back together. Identical retries left one metric; altered waveform retry failed without changing either side.
4. Terminating an uncommitted writer left neither row; retry on a fresh connection committed both.
5. Irregular telemetry inserted out of timestamp order worked. A minute aggregate stayed at count 2 / mean 3 after a late value 12, then changed to count 3 / mean 6 after explicit refresh.
6. Timescale-compressed metric rows joined to exact Morlet waveform intervals.
7. Explicit non-owner RLS reads worked on waveform parent/chunks and metric rowstore. Continuous-aggregate creation on an RLS hypertable and columnstore enablement on it were rejected (0A000). RLS enabled after aggregate creation was accepted; no aggregate was granted to a tenant, so aggregate authorization is NOT established.
8. Dropping telemetry chunks left Morlet samples unchanged. Refreshing the deleted source range removed the previously retained aggregate.
9. Orderly restart and same-server logical dump/restore using Timescale pre/post hooks preserved samples and compressed metrics.
10. Supplemental exact search over two 8192-sample recordings returned the identical 0..4096 match, distance 0, with exact raw read-back, including after restart/restore.
11. Supplemental bridge probes: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING silently ignored a changed metric payload; bigint timestamps 3 ns apart remained distinct while their timestamptz display projections collapsed.

The final run has 12 passing case groups, including diagnostics of unsupported combinations. First attempt retained: Docker changed the random host port after restart, causing harness readiness and restore-connection failures. Rediscovering the port fixed the harness; the unchanged core protocol then passed. Supplemental probes were frozen separately after that run.

## Proposed integration
- Morlet managed tables remain ordinary tables; no automatic conversion to hypertables.
- Raw waveforms stay in MorletDB; ordinary telemetry and small derived metric rows live in Timescale hypertables.
- Shared asset identities and explicit interval references support dashboard-to-waveform drill-down.
- Timescale remains optional; portable crates and the base Morlet workflow gain no dependency.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Publish a reproducible example and optional CI job with pinned compatible builds, both install orders, transaction/retry tests, exact read/search, permission boundaries and restore.
- [ ] Add support documentation distinguishing tested coexistence from production workload support.
- [ ] Cover upgrades, pgvector coexistence, roles/global objects in cross-host restore, a nonempty retained aggregate, scheduled jobs and representative concurrent ingest/query/maintenance.
- [ ] Record the combined distribution's actual licensing and extension-version requirements; the experiment image was not published.
- [ ] Complete focused bridge, isolation, lifecycle and dashboard follow-ups.

Artifacts were prepared locally under evaluation/timescale_coexistence/ (PROTOCOL.md, ADDENDUM.md, Dockerfile, run.py and three timestamped result JSONs); they are not yet published in the repository. The evidence above is included here so this issue does not depend on a nonexistent artifact link. Latest run: 20261128T121444Z; core run: 20261128T121322Z.

Related: #159, #197, #201, #204, #287. No throughput, latency, scale, failover, power-loss or live Grafana UI result is claimed.

## Focused follow-ups
- [ ] #632 — TimescaleDB bridge: verified metric publication with exact time and waveform provenance
- [ ] #633 — TimescaleDB integration: define tenant isolation for aggregates and column storage
- [ ] #634 — TimescaleDB integration: coordinate aggregate freshness, retention and evidence availability
- [ ] #635 — Grafana + TimescaleDB: supported trend-to-waveform investigation example

title: TimescaleDB bridge: verified metric publication with exact time and waveform provenance
body:
## Evidence
TC1 (#631), PostgreSQL 17.12 + pg_morlet SQL 0.3.14 + TimescaleDB 2.31.0, showed that waveform append and derived-metric insertion can commit/rollback together. Compressed metric rows successfully joined to exact source intervals.

Two supplemental diagnostics exposed missing adapter contracts:
- A metric key (time, recording_id, start_sample, calculation_version) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING accepted a retry containing RMS=99 without error and silently kept the original sqrt(1.5). This is behavior of the prototype, NOT a shipped MorletDB bug.
- Epoch bigint values 1767225600000000000 and 1767225600000000003 remained two distinct timestamps in an integer-time hypertable; projecting them with to_timestamp(t::numeric / 1000000000) produced one distinct timestamptz value.

## Proposed scope
A supported SQL/SDK publication path for low-rate metrics derived from authoritative waveform intervals. Keep Timescale optional and use an ordinary PostgreSQL-compatible row contract so other sinks remain possible. Do not duplicate every waveform sample into rows.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Define identity: collection + recording + zero-based half-open interval + calculation/version/parameters; include source specification/interpretation and time-axis revision where applicable.
- [ ] Preserve exact source coordinates and nanosecond time; any microsecond dashboard projection is explicitly a projection, never the uniqueness key. Test bucket boundaries and anchored recordings without silent rounding.
- [ ] Identical source AND metric retries are no-ops; changed payload/specification under the same identity fails. Validate count/interval/units and source visibility. Do not copy the prototype's ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING as a conflict verifier.
- [ ] Provide one-transaction append/publication for cheap metrics and a bounded resumable asynchronous worker for expensive metrics, with received/materialized watermarks and explicit incomplete state.
- [ ] Test concurrent retries, rollback, terminated writer, resume, calculation-version changes and unavailable source data. Use independent expected statistics and signed-zero raw read-back.
- [ ] Test non-owner direct metric access separately from waveform access; an interval reference is not an authorization grant.
- [ ] Support SQL drill-down after Timescale compression and logical restore; preserve stored raw samples and provenance.
- [ ] Reuse existing SDK/statistics/builders; portable crates do not depend on PostgreSQL or Timescale.

Related: #159 (completion), #600 (interpretation revisions), #602 (versioned features). This is a bridge/product gap, not a new metric codec or resampling feature. TC1 artifacts are currently local; #631 contains versions, observations and limitations.

title: TimescaleDB integration: define tenant isolation for aggregates and column storage
body:
## Evidence
TC1 (#631) tested pg_morlet SQL 0.3.14 and TimescaleDB 2.31.0 on PostgreSQL 17.12. Explicit RLS restricted non-owner direct reads of Morlet recording/chunk tables and a Timescale metric rowstore to tenant a. Morlet's RLS helper was tested before and after enabling summaries/roll-ups; those roll-up tables were empty.

The supported-combination probes observed:
- CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... WITH (timescaledb.continuous) over an RLS-enabled hypertable failed with SQLSTATE 0A000: "cannot create continuous aggregate on hypertable with row security".
- ALTER TABLE ... SET (timescaledb.compress, timescaledb.compress_segmentby='tenant') on that RLS table failed with SQLSTATE 0A000: "columnstore cannot be used on table with row security".
- Creating an aggregate first and then enabling RLS on its source was accepted. This is NOT proof that aggregate reads inherit source policies. No aggregate was granted to the tenant during TC1.

These are documented compatibility limitations, not a vulnerability report. Upstream: https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/build/continuous-aggregates/create-a-continuous-aggregate

## Decision needed
Choose an explicit supported isolation architecture: RLS-protected rowstore without these features, tenant-isolated schemas/databases with reviewed grants, or a separately authorized aggregate serving layer. A GROUP BY tenant clause alone is not authorization. Do not simply disable source RLS to make the example run.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Document the supported feature/authorization matrix and unsupported combinations per tested Timescale version.
- [ ] Define who owns and refreshes aggregates and who may SELECT them; raw, derived and aggregate privileges must be intentional.
- [ ] Integration setup detects unsupported combinations and explains a supported alternative without changing permissions silently.
- [ ] Test non-owner roles and direct SQL on recordings, chunks, populated summaries, metric tables, aggregate surfaces and drill-down; cover both RLS/feature-enablement orders.
- [ ] Test tenant reassignment/revocation and metadata changes so stale materializations cannot be mistaken for a current policy check.
- [ ] Cover restore, schema grants and worker roles. Failed/forbidden reads must not fall back to unrestricted results.
- [ ] If further tests discover a suspected vulnerability, follow SECURITY.md privately rather than putting exploit details here.

Part of #631; coordinate with #194 and the metric bridge. This issue addresses the composition contract rather than expanding Morlet's existing RLS helper to take ownership of arbitrary Timescale objects.

title: TimescaleDB integration: coordinate aggregate freshness, retention and evidence availability
body:
## Measured behavior
In TC1 (#631), TimescaleDB 2.31.0 and pg_morlet SQL 0.3.14 shared PostgreSQL 17.12:
- Irregular readings at 00:00:10 (2) and 00:00:40 (4) yielded a materialized minute aggregate count=2, mean=3.
- Inserting a late reading at 00:00:25 (12) did not change that materialized result until refresh; it then became count=3, mean=6.
- drop_chunks on the telemetry source removed its old rows and left both the materialized aggregate and independent Morlet waveform initially intact.
- Explicitly refreshing the now-deleted source range removed that historical aggregate row.

The probe used materialized_only=true, explicit refresh_continuous_aggregate calls and drop_chunks; it did NOT test scheduled policy jobs or real-time aggregate mode. These observations are expected database semantics, not a data-loss bug.

## Product gap
A combined installation needs one understandable lifecycle contract. Independent defaults can make a dashboard stale or remove summaries that the operator expected to keep. A retained metric also does not prove its original waveform is still available.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Coordinate late-data/backfill refresh windows with source expiry; test retaining aggregates outside the refresh horizon and refreshing changed retained sources.
- [ ] Expose source progress, metric materialization, aggregate refresh range/time and failures separately. A successful append must not imply a fresh dashboard.
- [ ] Track metric-to-waveform dependencies and report raw available, pending, compacted/expired and inaccessible states without leaking hidden source information.
- [ ] Preserve authorized waveform retention/approval rules. Timescale retention on telemetry must not mutate Morlet managed tables or silently bypass existing approvals.
- [ ] Make lifecycle changes inspectable with a dry run showing affected data, retained summaries and evidence consequences.
- [ ] Test real scheduled jobs, late arrivals near retention boundaries, interruption/resume, compression, non-owner access, restore and repeated maintenance.
- [ ] Add operational metrics/runbook instructions for lag and conflicting policies.

Extends #204 rather than replacing generic retention work; coordinate #159, #197 and #287. Raw-to-cold archival remains its own concern. See #631 for frozen-run provenance and limitations.

title: Grafana + TimescaleDB: supported trend-to-waveform investigation example
body:
## Evidence
TC1 (#631) verified the SQL path: Timescale-compressed metric rows joined to Morlet recording/sample intervals and returned exact waveform bytes. Exact envelope search on two 8192-sample synthetic recordings returned the known 0..4096 match at distance 0; read-back and the search survived restart and logical restore.

This was SQL-level testing. No Grafana panels, alert evaluation, HTTP viewer links or user workflow were exercised.

## Proposed example
One optional PostgreSQL deployment with both extensions:
1. Irregular temperature/counter telemetry in Timescale hypertables.
2. High-rate vibration stored once in MorletDB.
3. Small derived RMS/peak rows with versioned source interval references.
4. Grafana trends and an alert/query result linking to the original waveform and similar-history investigation.

Reuse examples/grafana and the existing viewer. Keep metadata/asset joins in ordinary PostgreSQL tables; do not require duplicating waveforms into Timescale.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Reproducible synthetic collector/example with shared asset/channel identity, units and explicit UTC/time precision.
- [ ] Provisioned Grafana PostgreSQL datasource and panels for irregular telemetry, waveform-derived metrics and materialization freshness.
- [ ] Clicking a metric resolves the correct collection, recording and half-open sample interval; joins across acquisition/recording boundaries are tested.
- [ ] Follow-on exact/probe search is labelled accurately and can read original matches. No claim that similarity establishes a diagnosis.
- [ ] Missing, stale, pending and retained-summary-only cases are distinguishable; alert queries do not interpret missing evidence as a healthy value.
- [ ] Use restricted datasource/viewer roles and the isolation architecture chosen for #631; references and links confer no new access.
- [ ] Validate panels through Grafana's API and run a browser drill-down test, including escaped identifiers and unavailable source intervals.
- [ ] Document migration boundaries: retaining Timescale queries is supported by the example; Influx API/Flux compatibility is not implied.
- [ ] Exercise restore and a retention transition in the example before calling it a supported integration.

Related: #197, #574 and #572. Depends on the verified metric bridge and tenant-isolation work under #631. This is a workflow integration, not a second viewer or a new dashboard engine.
